Bounded fetching

A fetcher without limits is a denial of service you wrote yourself. The first bound that matters is size: a response can be arbitrarily large, and the server decides.

Why Content-Length is not a bound

The header is a claim. A server can send a small one and then a very large body, so a client that trusts it has no bound at all. Read the stream and stop counting.

  • Cap the bytes read, not the bytes kept.
  • Count redirects, and check each hop.
  • Give the whole operation a deadline.

The last one catches the case the other two miss: a server that sends one byte per second, forever, stays under every size cap there is.
